Inside Pope Leo XIV's Grueling Three-Country Visit
Pope Leo XIV Shows Resilience on South America Trip
spot: Pope Leo XIV has pressed forward with a demanding 12-day tour across Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru, just weeks after undergoing surgery to remove a lobe of his right lung.
content_html:
Key Developments

Pope Leo XIV has maintained a robust presence during his ongoing 12-day trip to South America, visiting Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru despite having a lung removed in October due to a lung cancer diagnosis. Traveling aboard the papal aircraft, journalists initially suspected health issues when Vatican officials abruptly canceled a scheduled press Q&A session during the flight from Argentina to Peru. However, Vatican communications head Maria Montserrat Alvarado dismissed concerns, noting that the pontiff was doing well.

Video footage later revealed that instead of speaking with reporters, the pope visited the cockpit and interacted with the air traffic control tower. Throughout the journey—which features a demanding schedule of 12 flights, two helicopter rides, nine Masses, and 36 speeches—Pope Leo has walked up and down stairs, ridden standing in the popemobile, blessed babies, and delivered homilies in a strong voice.

Key Takeaways

  • Pope Leo XIV completed rigorous travel across Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru shortly after October lung surgery.
  • Vatican officials canceled a midair press briefing, prompting brief health speculation before footage showed the pontiff active in the cockpit.
  • The exhausting 12-day itinerary includes 12 flights, nine Masses, and 36 speeches, which the pope has managed without visible difficulty.

Why It Matters

The rigorous tour highlights the physical demands placed on the papacy and tests the pontiff's resilience following a major oncological procedure. Because the Vatican is often scrutinized for its handling of health transparency, the pope's active participation in numerous public events, Masses, and youth vigils serves to reassure the global Catholic community regarding his leadership capability and stamina.
